chunks: And if not for when you entered your garden, you had said: 'What Allah willed; there is no power except with Allah.' If you see me less than you in wealth and children,

key_terms.لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ: There is no power except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What phrase should one recite when entering one's garden or property to acknowledge God's will?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the virtue of *al-ḥusn al-ẓann* (good opinion) and the necessity of acknowledging Allah’s will (*mashīʾah*) even in moments of personal abundance, contrasting the believer’s humility with the wealthy man’s arrogance. The phrase 'lā quwwata illā billāh' serves as a theological anchor, reminding the reader that all capacity and sustenance are divine gifts, a concept central to Shia spiritual ethics regarding gratitude (*shukr*) and recognition of divine power (*qudrah*).
